statement: We generalized the 2-Disjoint Connected Subgraphs problem, to a problem called 3-Disjoint Connected Subgraphs, where instead of partitioning the vertex set into two connected sets, we are required to partition it into three connected sets. We gave an algorithm for 3-Disjoint Connected Subgraphs running in time O? (1.88n ). We believe that this algorithm can be of independent interest and may find other algorithmic applications. We designed an algorithm for Path Contraction which breaks the O? (2n ) barrier. It was surprising that even for a simple problem like Path Contraction, there was no known algorithm that solves it faster than O? (2n ). Our algorithm for Path Contraction relied the fact that the number of (Q, a, b)-connected sets can be bounded by O? (2a+b−|Q| ). This gives us savings in the number of states that we consider, in our dynamic programming routine (for enumerating partial solutions). We designed four different algorithms for Path Contraction and used them for appropriate instances, to obtain the main algorithm for Path Contraction.
